definition: Help desk software that records each user problem or request, tracks who owns it and its status, and keeps the notes from first report to closure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Passing a ticket the current technician cannot resolve to a more experienced support tier, such as level 2 or 3, or to another team or vendor.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Ticket field that records how badly a problem affects the user's work, often rated low, medium, or high, so urgent issues are handled first.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Ticket field that classifies the problem type, such as password reset, hardware, or network, so it is routed to the right team and counted in reports.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Clear written updates added to a ticket while work continues, recording what has been tried so far so another technician can pick it up.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: The process of tracking, supervising, and auditing an organization's hardware and software through their life cycle, from purchase to retirement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Central repository of configuration items, such as hardware, installed software, and their relationships, used to track licenses and judge the impact of changes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Label with a unique number, often a barcode, QR code, or RFID chip, fixed to a device so inventory systems can identify and track it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: The purchasing process for hardware and software: identify the need, get quotes, gain budget approval, negotiate, order, receive, and later retire or replace.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: A seller's promise that a purchased product is free of defects and will work as described for a set period, after which repairs may cost extra.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Record started as soon as an incident is suspected and kept to its end, logging every fact, action, time, and person involved.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Plain-language document that gives the exact steps, in order, for a routine task such as installing an operating system or a software package.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Documented steps for loading a software package with set options, listing its version, 32- or 64-bit build, license, approved users, and allowed devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: List of tasks done when an employee joins, such as creating the domain account, issuing a device, granting building access, and reviewing policies.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: List of tasks done when an employee leaves, such as disabling (not deleting) the account, revoking access, and collecting company devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Searchable library of support articles, often from a vendor and found by article number or phrase, that explains how to install, configure, and fix products.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Contract in which a provider commits to measurable service standards, such as uptime percentage and response time, with penalties if it falls short.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

definition: Agreement between teams in the same organization that sets the response times, resolution times, and quality goals one team owes another.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: One-way legal contract that binds the receiving party to keep the owner's confidential information, such as trade secrets, private and use it only as agreed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Two-way confidentiality contract in which both parties share sensitive information and each promises to protect what the other discloses.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Contract a user must accept before using proprietary software, setting how the product may be used and limiting the vendor's liability.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Organization rules, often signed during onboarding, that define what employees may and may not do with company computers, networks, email, and data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Notice shown at login or when opening a system that reminds users of legal, privacy, or compliance rules and often requires acknowledgment before access.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

definition: Structured process for proposing, approving, testing, carrying out, and documenting changes to systems or procedures so that disruption is kept low.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Documented steps to undo a failed change and return a system to its original configuration.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Part of a change plan that makes and verifies copies of critical systems and data before work starts, so they can be restored if the change fails.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Trying a proposed change in an isolated copy of the production environment, often built from virtual machines, before applying it to live systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Person assigned to own a business process, answer questions about it, and act as the contact who must be consulted on any change affecting it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Document that starts the change process, listing the item to be altered, the reason, priority, plan, rollback steps, and expected duration.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Pre-approved, low-risk, routine modification that follows a set procedure and needs no extra board approval each time it is done.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Modification that is neither routine nor urgent, so it needs a full review, risk assessment, implementation plan, and board approval before work starts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Urgent modification made right away to fix a critical problem, using a faster approval path than usual, such as patching an actively exploited flaw.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Period, such as a product launch or quarter end, when no modifications are allowed except emergencies or approved exceptions, to keep systems stable.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Scheduled, agreed period, usually during off-peak hours, set aside for updates and other planned work so users are disrupted as little as possible.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Group of stakeholders from across the organization that meets regularly to review proposed changes and approve or deny them.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Review of a proposed change for possible failure or side effects on other systems, used to give it a low, moderate, or high risk level.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Final step in which the people who will use a changed system test it and confirm it meets their needs before it is signed off.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: Copies all selected data regardless of earlier jobs and clears the archive bits; it takes the longest but restores from a single set.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Copies only files changed since the last backup of any kind and clears archive bits, so a restore needs the full set plus each later job in order.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Copies all files changed since the last full backup without clearing archive bits, so it grows daily and a restore needs only the full plus the latest one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Complete backup set built by software that merges the last full backup with the later incremental jobs, without reading all data from the source again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Job that saves all selected data like a full one but leaves archive bits unchanged, so it does not disturb the regular schedule, often run before an upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

definition: File attribute set when a file is created or changed that tells backup software the file needs copying; full and incremental jobs clear it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Restoring backed-up data to its original location, writing over the current data there, for example after ransomware or file corruption.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Restoring backed-up data to a different folder, machine, or site, used when the original is unavailable or to compare old files with current ones.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Regularly restoring sample jobs to a test system and comparing the results with the original data, to prove the saved copies can actually be recovered.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Media rotation scheme with daily, weekly, and monthly sets, where the last daily of the week is promoted to weekly and the last weekly to monthly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Guideline to keep three copies of data, counting the original, on two different types of media, with one copy stored offsite.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Copy of data kept at a different physical location or in the cloud, so it survives a fire, flood, or theft that destroys the main site.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

definition: Sudden flow of static electricity between objects at different voltages; as little as about 30 volts can damage a computer part without visible signs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Band worn by a technician and clipped to ground or the case, with about a 1-megohm resistor, that keeps the body at the same potential as the equipment.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Grounded work surface on which a computer or its parts are placed, and to which a technician can connect, so static charge drains safely away.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Shielding package, usually silver or pink, used to store and ship cards and boards; charges collect on its outside rather than reaching the parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

definition: Touching bare metal on the computer case before handling parts to equalize charge when no strap or mat is available; less effective than proper gear.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Connecting equipment and network racks to earth through low-gauge wire or bonding bars so stray current has a safe path away from people.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Routing, bundling, and tying cables away from walkways and high-traffic areas so they do not cause trips or get damaged.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Bending at the knees, keeping the back straight and the load close, and lifting with the legs; get help for loads over a quarter of body weight.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Fire suppressor rated for electrical fires, such as a burning power supply; common CO2 BC units work but can harm computer parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Protective eyewear worn when blowing out dust, cutting cable, or working where debris or chemicals could reach the eyes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Face covering worn while cleaning dusty computers or handling toner so that airborne particles are not breathed in.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

definition: Document for a chemical product, such as toner or a cleaner, that covers its hazards, first aid, spill handling, storage, and disposal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Discarded computers, phones, batteries, and toner cartridges, which contain heavy metals or chemicals and must be recycled under local or EPA rules, not trashed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Measure of moisture in the air; about 20 to 60 percent is advised, since dry air raises the risk of static discharge and damp air causes condensation.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Pressurized gas sprayed to blow dust out of fans, heat sinks, and keyboards, ideally outdoors or with a vacuum collecting the debris.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Very fine filter used in air cleaners and computer vacuums to trap dust and other tiny airborne particles in repair areas.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Unexpected rise in line voltage that lasts longer than a brief transient and can damage connected electronics.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Very short, sharp jump in voltage lasting only nanoseconds, often from lightning or from power being restored after an outage.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Drop in line voltage that lasts long enough to dim lights and can make computers shut off, while some power still flows.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Complete loss of electrical power for a prolonged period, often followed by a damaging jump in voltage when it returns.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Power strip with metal-oxide varistors, rated in joules, that diverts voltage spikes away from devices but gives no power during an outage.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Device with a battery that conditions incoming power and keeps equipment running for a few minutes during sags, brownouts, and blackouts so it can shut down safely.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls

definition: Block of outlets that lets several devices share one wall socket but, unless it has varistors, offers no protection from voltage spikes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

definition: The steps followed when a security breach or prohibited activity is found: identify it, report and escalate, preserve evidence, and document everything.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Chronological, signed record of everyone who handled a piece of evidence, when, and how it was stored, proving it was not altered.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Ranking of evidence by how quickly it disappears, so short-lived data such as RAM contents is collected before stable data on disks or archives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Exact duplicate of a storage device's contents made during an investigation so the evidence is preserved and examined without changing the original.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Material such as pirated software, malware, stolen data, or inappropriate images whose discovery on a system must be reported to a supervisor and, if needed, police.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Technical controls that restrict copying, sharing, or use of copyrighted software, music, video, and other digital content.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Software right that is genuine, not counterfeit, and still within its term, so the product may legally be activated and used.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: One-time purchase that lets you use a software version forever, though upgrades after the first year usually need a separate maintenance fee.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Software right bought by an individual for home use on their own device, such as a retail copy of Windows Home, not for business deployment.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Software right bought in bulk by an organization that allows installation on many company devices, often through a site or volume agreement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Terms, such as the GNU GPL, that let anyone use, study, modify, and redistribute software whose source code is published.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Identity data found on official documents such as passports, driver's licenses, birth certificates, Social Security cards, and taxpayer ID numbers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

definition: Patient medical and billing records that identify a person and are protected in the United States by the HIPAA Privacy Rule.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

term: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
definition: Card industry rules, enforced by banks rather than government, for how merchants must store, process, and protect credit and debit card data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: European Union law that protects the personal data of people in the EU, requiring consent and a right to erasure, even for companies outside Europe.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Legal and internal rules that set how long records such as financial transactions must be kept and when they must be destroyed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

definition: Giving the customer full attention, taking notes, and letting them finish without interruption so you fully understand the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: A question that cannot be answered with yes or no, such as asking what happens when the user prints, used to draw out details and narrow an issue.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Repeating the customer's problem back in your own words to confirm you understood it correctly before you begin work.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Technical terms and acronyms, such as WPA3 or TCP/IP, that a nontechnical customer may not understand and that should be avoided or explained simply.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Contacting the customer some time after a repair is finished to verify that the problem stayed fixed and that they are satisfied.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Dress such as a suit, traditionally black or navy, expected in settings like job interviews or executive meetings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Everyday office dress, such as slacks with a collared shirt or blouse, recommended for most on-site work and service calls.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Awareness of and respect for customers' different backgrounds and customs, including using their proper titles and checking that you understand each other.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Arriving at the agreed time and, if you will be late, contacting the customer ahead of time to apologize and give a new arrival time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Telling the customer how long a repair should take, what it involves, and when they will get status updates, then keeping to that timeline.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

definition: Windows script with a .bat extension, run by the Command Prompt, that executes a list of commands such as net use for mapping drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 63: Basic Scripting, Part II

definition: Windows script with a .ps1 extension that runs cmdlets such as New-LocalUser and uses names that begin with a dollar sign to hold values.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 63: Basic Scripting, Part II

definition: Older object-based Microsoft language saved with a .vbs extension, historically used in Windows and Office automation and now mostly replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 63: Basic Scripting, Part II

definition: Linux or UNIX script with a .sh extension that usually starts with #!/bin/bash and must be made executable with chmod +x before it runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 63: Basic Scripting, Part II

definition: Language saved in .js files that mainly controls how web pages behave, such as quizzes or calculators, and uses // for single-line notes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 63: Basic Scripting, Part II

definition: General-purpose, object-oriented language run by an interpreter, saved in .py files, and able to import ready-made modules such as random.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 63: Basic Scripting, Part II

definition: Named label in a script, such as $i or count, that holds a value like a number, text, or array that can change while the script runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 62: Basic Scripting, Part I

definition: Operating system setting with a name, such as Path or %username%, that scripts and programs can read to find folders and user details.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 62: Basic Scripting, Part I

definition: Line of notes in a script that is ignored when it runs, marked with # in PowerShell and Bash or // in JavaScript.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 62: Basic Scripting, Part I

definition: Construct that repeats a block of code a set number of times, using a counter that is initialized, tested, and incremented on each pass.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 62: Basic Scripting, Part I

definition: Branching construct that runs a block of code only when a condition is true and can run an else block when it is false.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Open, cross-platform screen-sharing system, such as RealVNC, that uses TCP port 5900 and is not encrypted by default.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Agent-based software, often used by managed service providers, that watches the health of many endpoints and lets technicians patch and control them from one console.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

term: Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments
definition: Open protocol for reaching the desktops of virtual machines remotely, with keyboard, mouse, audio, and video, and optional TLS on each channel.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

definition: Microsoft's implementation of the SOAP-based WS-Management protocol, used to run commands and PowerShell scripts and collect management data on remote computers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

definition: Built-in Windows 11 tool where a helper signs in, gets a six-digit code, and the user enters it to share or hand over control of their screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Third-party tools such as TeamViewer or Splashtop that let one person view another's desktop, usually to troubleshoot a problem together.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Tools such as OneDrive, Dropbox, or Google Drive used to move or share files between users and computers rather than to control a desktop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Remote-control agent installed on a computer and left waiting for incoming connections, so technicians can manage it at any time; keep it patched and use MFA.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: False or made-up output, such as invented citations or links, that a generative model presents confidently as fact because of gaps in its training data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 65: Appropriate Use of Artificial Intelligence

definition: Unfair results caused by how a model's design or assumptions favor certain outcomes, such as weighting efficiency over fairness.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Skewed model results caused by training data that does not fairly represent the real people or situations the system will face.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Presenting someone else's work as your own, a risk when generated text copies material that other people uploaded or published.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 65: Appropriate Use of Artificial Intelligence

definition: Practice of having people review and correct a model's outputs before they are used, to catch errors and fabricated answers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Computer systems that learn patterns from training data to recognize, predict, or generate text, images, and code, as in assistants like Copilot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 65: Appropriate Use of Artificial Intelligence

definition: Openly available hosted model service whose provider may keep and learn from what users enter, so confidential code or data must never be pasted in.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Model service run in an organization's own controlled environment, or under a data-protection agreement, so prompts and company data are not shared or used to train others.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

definition: Building generative features directly into everyday software, such as Copilot in Microsoft 365 summarizing meetings or drafting documents from files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 65: Appropriate Use of Artificial Intelligence

definition: Accidental exposure of confidential information, such as when staff paste source code or meeting notes into a public chatbot that may reuse it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence
